Climatology and anomaly of a variable for each field

Source: R/analysis.R
fpc_climatology.Rd

fpc_climatology() computes, for each field and each 5-day period of the year, the mean of the observed values in the reference years. fpc_anomaly() subtracts it from the values. Only observed values enter the climatology: read the composites with observed_only = TRUE.

Usage

fpc_climatology(x, var, ref_years = NULL, min_years = 2)

fpc_anomaly(x, var, ref_years = NULL, min_years = 2)

Arguments

x

A data frame from fpc_composites() (wide format).

var

Variable name.

ref_years

Years that define the climatology. NULL uses every year in x.

min_years

Minimum number of observed years for a period's climatology; fewer gives NA.

Value

fpc_climatology(): a data frame with field_id, period (1-73), clim and n_years. fpc_anomaly(): x with the columns period, clim and anomaly.

Details

Periods are numbered from 1 to 73 within each year (the 5-day calendar is anchored on 1 January 2016 and runs continuously, so a period's position in the year shifts by one day in leap years; period 74, when present, is merged into 73).

Examples

d <- fpc_example_dir()
x <- fpc_composites(vars = "ndvi", dir = d)
a <- fpc_anomaly(x, "ndvi", ref_years = 2021:2022)
summary(a$anomaly[format(a$date, "%Y") == "2023"])
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.       NAs 
#> -0.169143 -0.052251 -0.008422 -0.007676  0.030984  0.198953       568
